In a recent interview with Ross Coulthart, a retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, opens up about a warning email that he received related to the declassified UFO footage. The email contained the now-declassified UFO footage, which led to an array of confusion. In the interview, Tim Gallaudet notes that during an exercise that took place off the US East Coast, aviators were seeing UAP warnings.

He also points out the names of the aviators while discussing the situation during the interview. Gallaudet added in the interview that he did not know about this situation until he received the email on the Navy Secret Network. He spoke about what they went through during that particular situation, as the email with the declassified UFO footage pointed out that they "might have to shut down the exercise”

Retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, on declassified UFO footage

While speaking in the interview regarding the declassified UFO footage, retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet opens up about the email, which was quite alarming at that point. In the title of the email, it was written that there was an urgent safety-of-flight issue. The body of the email wanted to know more about the situation, as they were having numerous “midair collisions,” and they “might have to shut down the exercise”.

The email also included the declassified UFO footage, which has gained public attention in recent times. When Tim Gallaudet saw the UFO footage, his “socks were knocked off” as he had never seen something of that sort. He also added that he was not “read into the programs”. However, right after he saw the UFO footage, he knew that it was not them, as they did not do “test and development in training ranges”.

He also continues explaining the reason behind not doing “test and development in training ranges,” as it is “compressed” and is a “stressful” situation. Hence, there is no room to “mess around”. Tim Gallaudet also spoke about the “performance characteristics of the technology” that the observers saw, which is not something that could be designed by them.

Further discussing the declassified footage along with the warning email that retired Navy admiral Tim Gallaudet received, Gallaudet pointed out that the message was received from the operations officer. This particular operations officer worked for a “commander who was a four-star”. The operations officer was also a “two-star”. The email was sent to all the subordinate commanders ranging from one-star to two-star, along with senior executives.

As soon as they received the now-declassified footage, they were all alert and were able to understand that it was a “big deal”. Things took a turn when the email was “wiped” from Gallaudet’s computer, and he was never able to see it again. Even at the meetings that he attended every month, “no one talked about it”.

When questioned about why he did not question it, Gallaudet noted that even though he should have done so, he understood that it was “damage control,” because the classified data was not supposed to be sent to their computers. Gallaudet also added that he had come out with the truth because “people had to basically shut up about it” and the pilots also had to “mitigate the safety threat on their own”.
